patients_and_assay: About 20% of 112 Friedreich ataxia patients carry one composite allele, usually with a pure GAA allele in trans (nanopore genomes and amplicons); 22-342 GGA triplets (median 44) near the 5' end of the GAA tract
notes: FXN is on the + strand, so the structure is as written. The minor non-triplet G/A interruptions of another ~10% of patients are not sized in the paper and are left pure.

patients_and_assay: TCTG block of more than 75 units in 139/168 DM2 patients (TCTG repeat-primed PCR) and in 88/100 (repeat-primed PCR and Sanger); 40-8000 bp (10-2000 units) of TCTG beside 100-12,000 CCTG units in 7/9 (Cas9-enriched nanopore), whose per-patient ranges, e.g. (CCTG)100-4000(TCTG)0-1000, put the TCTG block's share anywhere from about 1% to 90% of the allele
notes: CNBP is on the - strand: the gene's (CCTG)n(TCTG)m is (CAGA)m(CAGG)n on the + strand. The papers find no other motif inside the CCTG tract.

patients_and_assay: (AAAGG)10-25(AAGGG)exp(AAAGG)4-6 as first described in Maori CANVAS patients; on 6 of 74 alleles of 37 RFC1 patients in an Australasian cohort (repeat-primed PCR and nanopore); none of 84 alleles of 42 German RFC1 patients (40 biallelic AAGGG, 2 with an (AAAGG)>500 allele; Cas9-targeted nanopore); 6 of 158 alleles pooled
notes: The papers write the repeat as AAGGG, on the + strand (the Alu's sense strand), in this block order. The Australasian cohort's paper restates the allele as (AAAGG)15-25(AAGGG)exp(AAAGG)10; the block counts here are the first description's, as STRchive quotes it.

patients_and_assay: Mixed ATTCT and ATTCC in all 5 affected expansion carriers of one kindred, whose 6 pure-ATTCT carriers were unaffected or had Parkinson disease (amplification-free PacBio); 6/6 Peruvian index cases (Cas9-targeted long reads); 1/3 sequenced patients (SMRT; the other two carry ATTCTTCT/ATTCTCT or ATCCT/ATCCC interruptions); both SCA10 patients of a German cohort, (ATTCT)~130(ATTCC)~1400 (Cas9-targeted nanopore): 14 of 16 patients, ATTCC from about 9% to 92% of the allele
notes: ATXN10 is on the + strand. The ATTCC block goes 3' of the ATTCT tract, the layout most often reported; some alleles hold it centrally or interspersed. The German cohort's paper calls pure ATTCT the typical SCA10 allele, though its own patients carry mostly ATTCC.

patients_and_assay: The only configuration in 36/36 FAME1 patients (long-range PCR and deep PacBio HiFi): TTTCA 1.2-62.6% of a 526-1226 unit repeat
notes: SAMD12 is on the - strand: the gene's (TTTTA)exp(TTTCA)exp is (TGAAA)exp(TAAAA)exp on the + strand, written here in the locus's AAAAT phase. No patient carries a pure TTTCA tract.

patients_and_assay: 16/16 FAME3 patients (repeat-primed PCR, nanopore genomes, molecular combing): 5' TTTTA 0.6-3.5 kb, TTTCA 2-10.4 kb, 3' TTTTA 0.3-1.3 kb; per patient (combing of blood, 9 patients), TTTCA 35-75% and the 3' TTTTA 5-20% of the allele
notes: MARCHF6 is on the + strand, written here in the locus's ATTTT phase.

patients_and_assay: Interrupted alleles in 3-8% of DM1 patients, mostly CCG or CCGCTG at the 3' end, e.g. (CTG)n(CCGCTG)(CTG)7(CCGCTG)(CTG)11 (PacBio Sequel II amplicons, triplet-primed PCR, review of 25 families)
notes: DMPK is on the - strand: (CTG)n(CCGCTG)(CTG)7(CCGCTG)(CTG)11 is (CAG)11(CAGCGG)(CAG)7(CAGCGG)(CAG)n on the + strand.

patients_and_assay: 6 of 9 full-mutation alleles (8 people) of a reference panel kept one AGG 9-10 CGG from the 5' end; 3 (505-900 CGG) had none (long-range PCR and PacBio HiFi)
notes: FMR1 is on the + strand. A small sample.

patients_and_assay: 11/11 SCA37 patients of 8 kindreds, 5' (ATTTT)57-76 then the pathogenic (ATTTC)47-78 then 3' (ATTTT)75-91 (Cas9-enriched nanopore, long-range PCR and Sanger); STRchive adds that pathogenicity needs more than 30 pathogenic copies flanked by at least 58 reference copies on either side
notes: DAB1 is on the - strand, so the gene's three blocks read (AAAAT)(GAAAT)(AAAAT) on the + strand in the reverse order. STRchive's pathogenic sizes count only the pathogenic block, so the simulated size is that block's and the reference blocks are added to it.

structure: insertion behind a short TAGAA block
patients_and_assay: 94/94 SCA31 patients of 71 families carry the insertion, whose 5' end holds 1 to 4 TAGAA copies before the pathogenic TGGAA tract (long PCR, HaeIII and Sanger of the 5' end): 1 copy in 50 patients, 2 in 20, 3 in 14, 4 in 8, none in 2
notes: BEAN1 is on the + strand. STRchive's pathogenic sizes count the pure TGGAA tract inside the insertion, so the simulated size is that block's and the TAGAA block is added to it. A nanopore study finds TAGAA and TAAAA copies making up about half of the whole insertion (10.1038/s41525-022-00331-y) without saying where they sit, so only the 5' block is simulated.

patients_and_assay: 158/158 affected of 22 families positive by repeat-primed PCR from both ends; 3 spanning long reads of 2 patients (PacBio and nanopore of fibroblast DNA) read as the pathogenic block then the reference block, with 274-588 pathogenic and 340-390 reference copies
notes: The paper writes the two blocks on the + strand of chr2 in this order and this phase. STRchive's pathogenic sizes count only the pathogenic block, so the simulated size is that block's and the reference block is added to it.

patients_and_assay: The one reported family's allele is 22 reference copies, then the pathogenic block of about 1,100 copies, then an expanded reference block of unsaid length; the same study found the reference block expanded to 40-120 copies in nine healthy people
notes: TNRC6A is on the + strand, the blocks in this order. STRchive's pathogenic sizes count only the pathogenic block, so the simulated size is that block's and the reference blocks are added to it. No patient's 3' block length is published, so it is drawn from the healthy people's range.

patients_and_assay: A Japanese sporadic case and a Chinese family; the structure is an expanded reference block, then the pathogenic block of 60 to a few thousand copies, then more reference copies, of which only the pathogenic block is specific to patients (reviews of the familial adult myoclonic epilepsy loci and STRchive's reading of the two reports)
notes: RAPGEF2 is on the + strand, the blocks in this order. STRchive's pathogenic sizes count only the pathogenic block, so the simulated size is that block's and the reference blocks are added to it. No patient's reference-block length is published, so both are the 18 copies of the reference allele at this locus, a lower bound.

patients_and_assay: One reported family, an insertion of about 1,000 pathogenic copies in the reference repeat, of which only the pathogenic block is specific to patients (reviews of the familial adult myoclonic epilepsy loci and STRchive's reading of the report)
notes: YEATS2 is on the + strand, the blocks in this order. STRchive's pathogenic sizes count only the pathogenic block, so the simulated size is that block's and the reference blocks are added to it. No patient's reference-block length is published, so both are the 7 copies of the reference allele at this locus, a lower bound.
